texts.preamble: Sh. Manoj Rathi vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 11 May, 2016 1 In The Court Of Sh. Rakesh Pandit, Asj-01, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Case Id No.02403R0075742014 Ca No. 27/16 Sh. Manoj Rathi S/o Sh. Om Prakash Rathi M/s Maheshwari Store, M-3, Panchsheel Garden, Naveen Shahdara, Delhi-32 R/o 1/10056-B, West Gorakh Park, Gali no. 5, Delhi-110032. ....A Vs. The State (Delhi Administration) Pfa Department, A-20 Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi. .... Date of receiving of Appeal : 24.02.2016 Date of arguments : 19.04.2016 Date of judgment : 11.05.2016 Judgment
texts.facts: 2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s CA No. 27/16 Manoj Rathi Vs. State page 1 of 7 Maheshwari Store, M-3, Panchsheel Garden, Naveen Sahadara, New Delhi. On 26.04.2004 at about 6.00 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. Ram Pratap Singh visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Dal Arhar" (ready for sale) from accused. FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. R. K. Chauhan. The said Arhar Dal was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act. The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA. Panchanama was prepared. One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst. As Sh. Manoj Rathi vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 11 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111957838/ 1 per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine." 3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 10.08.2004 with the court. Accused was summoned. He has not exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL. 4 Charge was framed against accused u / sec.2(ia) (a) (j) (m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act. 6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:- CA No. 27/16 Manoj Rathi Vs. State (i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule independent witnesses were not joined. (ii) Non-compliance of Sec.17 & 18 Of PFA Rules. (iii) PA report was not signed on the day of analysis. (iv) The adulteration of Dal Arhar falls in the category of misbranding and not adulteration. (v) Public Analyst was not appointed as PA on the date of sampling. (vi) Paper chromatography test is not a reliable test. (vii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official. 7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
texts.arguments: 9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor Sh. Manoj Rathi vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 11 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111957838/ 2 It is CA No. 27/16 Manoj Rathi Vs. State page 4 of 7 further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts. However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food. If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis. So, the Hon. Supreme Court use Sh. Manoj Rathi vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 11 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111957838/ 3 the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers". Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean. Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean. Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry. 16 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be CA No. 27/16 Manoj Rathi Vs. State crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample. 18 PW2/LHA R. K. Chauha also deposed that the jhaba was provided by the accused in clean and dry condition.
